judgment.notes: M011 at S002 is instantiated with X=ℝ, Q=Measure ℝ on its Borel structure, ν=λ, T=ℕ and B_i=J_i. N005 applies separately to each nonempty W_i: its diameter ρ_i is finite, 0≤ρ_i≤δ, and η=ε2^{-i-1}>0. Empty members use λ(∅)=0 instead. N001's power limits are used only with a-1>0 and s-1<0; its dimension implications are used with positive exponents and the same Euclidean set I. Routine power applications and all their signs are checked in BG002–BG004 and BG006–BG009. There are no E applications.

S001's equal-interval covers have mesh 1/m and total cost m(1/m)^a=(1/m)^{a-1}; BG001–BG004 verify the finite construction, power identities and reciprocal mesh step. N001 supplies convergence of that cost to zero, so at every fixed scale the content is zero; its supremum is zero. The critical-exponent implication gives dim_H(I)≤a for every a>1, hence ≤1. S002's N005 enclosures really cover W_i, have positive errors and cover I. Monotonicity, λ(I)=1 and M011 give the union/series inequality. For every finite initial sum its error term is at most ε using N001's geometric sum, so the supremum is ≤Σρ_i+ε. If this sum is finite and below 1, ε=(1-Σρ_i)/2 contradicts the inequality; if infinite the bound ≥1 is automatic. S003 uses the correctly directed negative-power comparison, handles zero diameters separately, and sums a pointwise cost inequality with a finite positive multiplier. From the supremum definition of series, multiplication by this scalar preserves suprema (divide any finite candidate upper bound by the scalar; unbounded partial sums remain unbounded). Thus every admissible cover has cost ≥δ^{s-1}, and taking the infimum preserves this bound. The bound for arbitrary δ and N001's negative-power divergence imply H^s(I)=∞, then dim_H(I)≥s for all 0<s<1 and hence ≥1. Extended-infinite sums and zero diameters cause no lost case. This follows the supplied route, with only recorded routine background.
